newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks set 7-yr peak despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks set 7-yr peak despite profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed at another seven-year high on Thursday despite late profit-taking triggered by a strong technical resistance that formed following recent torrential gains, brokers said.
The weighted index had soared to a seven-year intra-day high of 9,511.80 but lost some steam in late trade to finish 67.06 points or 0.72 percent higher at 9,429.74.
The close still surpassed the 9,415.58 finish on Wednesday and was the index's highest level since it closed at 9,665.50 on April 28, 1990.

The 9,429.74 finish was more than twice the index's 4,692.40 close on March 12, 1996 that came amid foundering market confidence induced by China's war games near the Taiwan Strait ahead of Taiwan's presidential election on March 23 that year.
Turnover on Thursday was a voluminous T$220 billion, though still below the all-time high of T$251 billion registered on June 19.
Brokers said Thursday's gains were guided by a rare simultaneous rise of the market's two most heavily weighted sectors -- financials and electronics.
"When you see this dual mainstreaming, both sectors rising at the same time, you know how bullish the market is now," said National Securities analyst Alex Yang.
Yang added that sentiment was buoyed further by strong performance of high-tech shares in the U.S. Nasdaq market, even though Wall Street as a whole stumbled on Wednesday.
Electronics, solidifying as the market bellwether and often clocking 60 percent of daily turnover, rose 0.83 percent.
No.2 chipmaker United Microelectronics rose T$3.50 to T$140 after hiring the ex-president of No.1 maker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.
